Netflix spent $17 billion on content in 2025. What did it buy? A library that runs the entire ideological spectrum from STRONGLY WOKE to STRONGLY TRADITIONAL, often on the same platform, sometimes in the same month. We have scored 48 Netflix Originals -- films and series produced or exclusively distributed by the streaming giant -- and the results are more interesting than either the "Netflix is woke" or "Netflix is fine" camps would have you believe.

The platform has exactly one STRONGLY WOKE title: Emilia Pérez, Jacques Audiard's Spanish-language musical about a cartel boss who transitions to live as a woman. At -25.4 margin, it is in a category by itself. But the WOKE LEAN tier is the real story. Thirteen Netflix Originals land there, from Enola Holmes 3 (-8.7) to Ozark (-4.0). These are not fringe experiments. They are flagship properties: Stranger Things, Wednesday, Bridgerton, Squid Game. The platform's most visible content carries a consistent progressive tilt, even if it rarely reaches the ideological intensity of theatrical releases.

What Netflix does that no theatrical studio can match is balance. The MIXED tier (seven titles) and the TRADITIONAL LEAN tier (fourteen titles) together represent nearly half the catalog. The Gray Man (+6.5), Extraction 2 (+12.8), and Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F (+11.2) are action films that do not apologize for their traditional architecture. The STRONGLY TRADITIONAL tier is anchored by Happy Gilmore 2 (+27.8), War Machine (+26.5), Cobra Kai (+23.1), and Stranger Things Season 1 (+21.3) -- four titles that would crack the top tier of any traditional ranking.

Netflix's content strategy is not ideological. It is algorithmic. The platform serves different audiences different products, and the ideological diversity is a feature of that model, not a bug. But the pattern is clear: the prestige content -- the awards contenders, the buzzy dramas, the shows that drive cultural conversation -- leans woke. The popcorn content leans traditional. Parents who trust the Netflix brand should understand which category each title falls into before pressing play. Ranked from most woke to most traditional.

STRONGLY WOKE (Margin -25.4)

#1: Emilia Pérez (2024)

Woke Score: 30.4 • Traditional Score: 5.0 • Verdict: STRONGLY WOKE • Margin: -25.4

Genre: Musical/Crime/Drama | Platform: Netflix

Jacques Audiard's Spanish-language musical about a Mexican cartel boss who transitions to live as a woman is the most ideologically aggressive Netflix Original in our database. Emilia Pérez is not a film that contains progressive messaging. It is a film that is progressive messaging, wrapped in the formal audacity of a musical and the prestige of an international auteur. Karla Sofía Gascón's performance earned a Best Actress prize at Cannes, and the film's festival trajectory suggests the industry is fully aligned with its thesis. At 30.4 woke to just 5.0 traditional, the margin of -25.4 is not close. The traditional score of 5.0 reflects some residual crime-drama architecture -- loyalty, codes of honor, the cost of violence -- but these elements exist in service of the film's central argument about identity, transformation, and the rejection of masculine violence. Parents should know: this is not a crime film with progressive elements. It is a progressive film that uses crime-genre scaffolding.

WOKE LEAN (Margin -4.0 to -8.7)

#2: Enola Holmes 3 (2026)

Woke Score: 16.1 • Traditional Score: 7.4 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -8.7

Genre: Mystery / Adventure | Platform: Netflix

The Enola Holmes franchise completes its pivot from charming Victorian detective romp into something heavier and more politically pointed. Millie Bobby Brown remains the franchise's greatest asset, but the film's ideological project has moved from the margins to the center: marriage is framed as a threat to female autonomy, the mystery involves systemic injustice rather than individual crime, and the resolution prioritizes Enola's independence over romantic fulfillment. At 16.1 woke to 7.4 traditional, the margin reflects a franchise that started as light entertainment and has grown heavier with each installment.

#3: Adolescence (2025)

Woke Score: 22.5 • Traditional Score: 14.8 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -7.8

Genre: Psychological Crime Drama | Platform: Netflix

Adolescence is a psychological crime drama that examines the circumstances surrounding a teenage boy accused of murder. The series interrogates contemporary anxieties about masculinity, online radicalization, and the vulnerability of young men to toxic influences. At 22.5 woke to 14.8 traditional, the margin of -7.8 reflects a show that is genuinely interested in complexity -- the traditional score is substantial because the series does not simply condemn its subject but attempts to understand the forces that shaped him. Parents should know the thematic territory is dark and the ideological framework is progressive.

The later seasons of Stranger Things tell an interesting story about how a show evolves ideologically over time. The franchise that began as the most traditional thing Netflix had ever made has drifted left, and the -5.0 margin at this point in the series reflects that drift.

The Takeaway

Forty-eight Netflix Originals, scored and ranked. The ideological distribution is not what either the "Netflix is woke" or "Netflix is fine" narratives would predict. The platform has exactly one STRONGLY WOKE title and four STRONGLY TRADITIONAL titles. The WOKE LEAN tier (thirteen entries) and the TRADITIONAL and TRADITIONAL LEAN tiers (twenty-four entries combined) tell the more interesting story. Netflix is not ideologically uniform. It is ideologically diverse in a way that no theatrical studio can match, precisely because it does not need to fill theaters -- it needs to fill subscriber niches.

But the diversity has a pattern. The prestige content -- the award contenders, the buzzy dramas that drive the cultural conversation -- leans woke. Emilia Pérez (-25.4), Adolescence (-7.8), Bridgerton (-6.2), Squid Game (-5.8). These are the titles Netflix promotes at festivals, submits for awards, and uses to define its brand. The popcorn content -- the action films, the comedies, the legacy sequels -- leans traditional. Happy Gilmore 2 (+27.8), War Machine (+26.5), Extraction 2 (+12.8), Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F (+11.2). These are the titles that generate the viewing hours, and they are built on traditional architecture that demands no ideological negotiation from the audience.

The WOKE LEAN tier is where the platform's most visible properties cluster. Stranger Things (-5.0), Wednesday (-5.5 and -5.7 for Season 2), Bridgerton (-6.2), Enola Holmes 3 (-8.7), Squid Game (-5.8), Ozark (-4.0). These are the shows your kids are watching and the shows driving Netflix's subscriber retention. The progressive tilt is consistent, if not extreme. Parents should be aware that the platform's most heavily promoted content carries an ideological signature that may not align with their values.

The franchise trajectory data tells its own story. Stranger Things opened at +21.3 STRONGLY TRADITIONAL in Season 1. It drifted to -5.0 WOKE LEAN by the later seasons before course-correcting to +7.8 TRADITIONAL LEAN in Season 5. That arc is a case study in how long-running series change ideologically as writers' rooms evolve, showrunners change, and the cultural moment shifts. Wednesday Season 1 scored -5.5 WOKE LEAN, and Season 2 deepened slightly to -5.7. Enola Holmes 3 at -8.7 is the endpoint of a franchise that started lighter on the politics. Parents who approved a show in Season 1 should not assume Season 3 is the same product.

The bottom of this list -- Happy Gilmore 2, War Machine, Cobra Kai, Stranger Things Season 1, Little House on the Prairie -- are not accidents. They are proof that Netflix can produce ideologically conservative content when it wants to, and that audiences reward it when it does. The question for the platform is not whether traditional content works. The question is whether Netflix is willing to make more of it, or whether the prestige impulse toward progressive messaging will continue to define the brand while the traditional content fills out the catalog.
